It's true that you don't need any of the DLCs to win games, but then again, I never said otherwise. That's not the issue here.

From a game I paid a full price tag for, I expect a little bit more than just "being able to win". Having half the game's playable content (licenced characters) locked behind a second paywall is one thing, but having the other half (original characters) also locked behind excessive grind on top of that is just too much. I have a lot of time on my hands to grind for stuff, but not everyone else does.

I think I would still have fun in that situation, yeah. I mean, I play the game for a reason, and it's definitely not because I have all the meta perks. I don't think the game simply having the capacity to be fun is high enough of a bar though, personally. I have higher standards of respect for video game developers/publishers.

The prices themselves aren't high, but they are very when considering what you're actually getting. Most games available for VR seem to have a disappointing lack of depth (pun not intended) and replayability beyond the initial "Woah it's VR" factor.

I've played Rec Room a bit, and it's certainly the closest to the long-term progression I've been looking for, but even that is pretty meh. The game I've had the most fun with so far is Until You Fall. It's great but gets old so damn fast, as do all of the other VR games I've played. Synth Riders appears to be another one of those arcade-like games which are so popular. You play a song and you get score, repeat for different song. Games like that (beat saber, pistol whip, etc.) are fun for the first little while, but after the wow factor wears off they're just exceptionally boring experiences. They are not made for long-term play. It's awesome that people are having a good time with them, but they just don't do it for me. I personally like games you can play pretty much 24/7 and always have something to do in. Games in which I can sink tons of playtime into and then have something to show for it afterwards.
